title: 1. Hook: The Ultimate Zoom
text: Have you ever looked at a drop of water and wondered what it's made of? If you zoomed in a million times, what would you see? Is it just smaller water, or something completely different?

title: 2. Socratic Thinking: The Cutting Experiment
text: Over 2500 years ago, an ancient Indian philosopher named Maharishi Kanad asked a simple question: If we take a piece of matter (Padarth) and keep breaking it into smaller and smaller pieces, will we ever reach a point where it cannot be broken anymore? What do you think?

content.title: 3. Discovery: The Invisible World
content.description: Imagine cutting a block of gold. As the pieces get microscopic, we reach a solid, unbreakable sphere.

title: 4. The Reveal: The Atom
text: That ultimate, unbreakable particle is called an **Atom**. The word comes from the Greek word *atomos*, meaning 'indivisible'. Maharishi Kanad called this ultimate particle **Parmanu** (Param = ultimate, anu = particle). Atoms are the building blocks of all matter.

question: According to Maharishi Kanad, what is the smallest indivisible particle of matter called?

title: 6. Reflection: Why can't we see them?
text: Explain in your own words: If everything is made of atoms, why can't we see a single atom even with a powerful magnifying glass?

title: 7. Connection: The Lego Bricks of the Universe
text: Think of atoms as the universe's Lego bricks. Just as you can build a spaceship, a castle, or a car using the same basic Lego pieces, the universe builds trees, stars, and humans using different combinations of atoms!

content.title: 8. Mastery: The Size of an Atom
content.text: Can you imagine the size of an atom? Try this: Take a single sheet of paper. It is about 1,000,000 (one million) atoms thick! Think about how tiny a single atom must be to fit a million of them in the thickness of paper.

title: 1. Hook: Lonely Atoms
text: We know everything is made of atoms. But most atoms don't like to stay alone. They are like lonely people looking for friends. What happens when atoms find each other?

title: 2. Socratic Thinking: Oxygen's Secret
text: The oxygen we breathe isn't just single oxygen atoms floating around. If it was, we couldn't breathe it! Why do you think oxygen atoms always travel in pairs?

content.title: 3. Discovery: Holding Hands
content.description: Watch two separate oxygen atoms come together and bond, forming a stable pair.

title: 4. The Reveal: Molecules
text: When two or more atoms chemically bond together, they form a **Molecule**. For example, two oxygen atoms bond to form an oxygen molecule (O2). A molecule is the smallest particle of a substance that can exist independently and show all properties of that substance.

content.text: Remember: Atoms are like the letters of the alphabet, and molecules are the words made from those letters!
Students often confuse atoms and molecules. An atom is a single particle (like 'O' for Oxygen). A molecule is a group (like 'O2' or 'H2O').

question: Which of the following represents a molecule of water?

title: 6. Reflection: Endless Combinations
text: If there are only about 118 types of atoms in the universe, how is it possible that there are millions of different substances like plastic, wood, water, and DNA?

title: 7. Connection: Life Itself
text: Your DNA, the code of your life, is just one giant, complex molecule made of millions of atoms working perfectly together.

content.title: 8. Mastery: Build a Molecule
content.text: Draw a water molecule (H2O). Hint: It looks like a famous cartoon mouse's head! One large oxygen atom in the center, and two smaller hydrogen atoms acting like ears.
